sources.source: Lower Bounds For Algebraic Computation Trees (M. Ben-Or, STOC 1983)

items.item: Abstract and 1. Introduction: topological method for algebraic computation trees; element distinctness as Example 1; Theorem 1 (Omega(n log n)).

at.step: Distinctness: every neighbour must be compared

items.item: 2. The algebraic computation tree model: membership problem for W, arithmetic operations and tests, complexity as maximum path length.
3. Counting connected components: Theorem 2 (Milnor-Thom bound on components of V).

at.out: the Milnor-Thom bound on the number of connected components is a topological tool, cited and not proved; the Deep dive states what it is used to count (n! components)

items.item: 4. Main theorem: Theorem 3 (2^h 3^(n+h) >= N) and Theorem 4 (C(W) >= log N / (1 + log 3)); extensions to k-th roots.

at.out: Theorems 3 and 4 and the k-th root extensions are the proof machinery for general algebraic trees, cited and not reproduced; Theorem 1 and the expected-time Theorem 11 are stated in the Deep dive

items.item: 5. Bounded degree algebraic decision trees; 6. applications including element distinctness; 7. ruler and compass constructions.
